cues.en: I realized recently that I didn't really understand how a prism works. The standard explanation, what you might hear in a high school physics class, for example, goes something like this.
cues.zh: 我最近意识到，我其实并不真正理解棱镜是如何工作的。比如你在高中物理课上可能听到的标准解释，大概是这样的。

cues.en: When light enters a medium like glass,
cues.zh: 当光进入像玻璃这样的介质时，

cues.en: it slows down in the sense that if you look at the crests of the wave in a vacuum, those crests are traveling at c, the speed of light. But inside the glass, those crests will be traveling a little bit slower.
cues.zh: 它会变慢，意思是如果你看真空中波的波峰，那些波峰以 c（光速）前进。但在玻璃内部，那些波峰前进得会稍微慢一点。

cues.en: And the specific ratio between the speed of light vacuum and the speed inside a medium like this is called the index of refraction
cues.zh: 而真空中光速与这种介质内部速度的具体比值，被称为折射率

cues.en: for that medium.
cues.zh: 也就是该介质的折射率。

cues.en: The reason we use the word refraction instead of say the index of slowing is that if a beam of light enters this glass at an angle,
cues.zh: 我们使用“折射”这个词，而不是说“减速指数”，原因是当一束光以某个角度进入玻璃时，

cues.en: then a consequence of this slowdown is that it bends a little bit or using the lingo, it refracts.
cues.zh: 那么这种减速的一个结果就是它会稍微弯折一下，或者用行话说，它发生了折射。

cues.en: And the way my high school physics teacher always explained this was to imagine a tank going from some region where it can travel relatively quickly like concrete into something slower like mud,
cues.zh: 我高中物理老师一直是这样解释的：想象一辆坦克从某个能走得相对较快的区域，比如混凝土，开进更慢的东西里，比如泥浆，

cues.en: where if it's coming in at an angle,
cues.zh: 如果它是斜着开进来的，

cues.en: then as one of its treads hits the slow region first,
cues.zh: 那么当它的一侧履带先碰到慢速区域时，

cues.en: that tread will be going slower while the other one is faster, causing the whole tank to steer a little bit until that second tread also enters the mud, then it continues straight just traveling a little slower.
cues.zh: 那条履带会走得更慢，而另一条更快，导致整辆坦克稍微转向，直到第二条履带也进入泥浆，然后它就继续直行，只是走得稍微慢一点。

cues.en: We'll get back to the actual reason for bending in a bit, but at this point, the high school physics students typically learn a law known as Snell's law, which specifies exactly how much things bend.
cues.zh: 我们稍后会回到光线发生偏折的真正原因，但在这之前，高中物理课通常会介绍一条叫作斯涅尔定律的规律，它能精确说明物体会偏折多少。

cues.en: If you draw a line perpendicular
cues.zh: 如果你画一条垂直于

cues.en: to the boundary between the glass and water and consider the angle between that perpendicular line and the beam of light, then Snell's law tells us that the sine of this angle divided by the speed of the light is always a constant.
cues.zh: 玻璃和水交界面的直线，再考虑这条垂线与光束之间的夹角，那么斯涅尔定律告诉我们，这个角的正弦除以光速后始终是一个常数。

cues.en: So the slower the light, the lower that angle will be, and that lets you actually calculate how much things refract.
cues.zh: 所以光速越慢，这个角就越小，这样你就能算出物体会发生多少折射。

cues.en: What's going on with a prism then is that the specific amount that light slows down depends a little bit on its frequency.
cues.zh: 棱镜的情况是，光速减慢的具体程度会在一定程度上取决于它的频率。

cues.en: For example, blue light, which has a relatively high frequency, would get slowed down more aggressively than red light, which has a relatively low frequency.
cues.zh: 例如，频率相对较高的蓝光，比频率相对较低的红光减速得更明显。

cues.en: Now most of the light that you see is not a clean pure sine wave. In particular, the white light coming from the sun is not a clean sine wave. It's something much messier, but it can be expressed as a sum of a bunch of clean sine waves, each one corresponding to a pure spectral color.
cues.zh: 现在，你看到的大多数光都不是干净的纯正弦波。尤其是来自太阳的白光，并不是干净的正弦波。它要复杂得多，但可以表示为许多干净正弦波的叠加，而每个正弦波都对应一种纯粹的光谱色。

cues.en: So when you shine white light into a prism like this, all those different components get refracted by slightly different amounts causing this iconic separation of the pure rainbow colors.
cues.zh: 所以，当你把白光照进这样的棱镜时，所有这些不同的成分都会发生程度略有不同的折射，从而形成这种标志性的纯彩虹色分离。

cues.en: So that is the standard explanation,
cues.zh: 所以这就是标准解释，

cues.en: and it's not wrong per se. It's just that all of the key components are handed down from on high. Like, why would light slow down like this? And what exactly do we mean by slowing down? And even if you understand that, why would the amount that it slows down have anything to do with the color of the light? Is that just a coincidence or is it necessary?
cues.zh: 它本身没错。只是所有关键部分都是自上而下灌输的。比如，光为什么会这样变慢？我们说的“变慢”到底指什么？就算你理解了这一点，为什么减慢的程度会和光的颜色有关？这只是巧合，还是必然？

cues.en: If you have a sufficiently high standard for explanations,
cues.zh: 如果你对解释有足够高的标准，

cues.en: you want both of these facts to feel discovered
cues.zh: 你会希望这两个事实都像是被发现的，

cues.en: rather than feeling like they were handed down.
cues.zh: 而不是像被灌输下来的。

cues.en: The first explanation I saw that started to give this feeling came from the Feynman lectures on the matter. And a lot of what I'd like to do with this video is simply animate a lot of the key points that he makes there. It involves really digging in to think about each individual wiggling charge in the material and the propagating light waves caused by each one of those charges and how all of them superimpose on top of each other, which feels like it should be a complete mess, but it actually works out to be not only understandable,
cues.zh: 我看到的第一个开始带来这种感觉的解释，来自 Feynman 关于这个问题的讲座。这个视频里我想做的很多事，就是把他讲到的很多关键点做成动画。这需要真正深入思考材料中每一个振动的电荷、每个电荷产生的传播光波，以及它们如何彼此叠加；这感觉应该会一团糟，但结果不仅可理解，

cues.en: but satisfyingly
cues.zh: 而且令人满意地

cues.en: explanatory.
cues.zh: 具有解释力。

cues.en: For example, it explains why it has to depend on color, and the key intuition there really comes down to what happens if you're bad at pushing a child on a swing. Bear with me. I promise that'll make sense later.
cues.zh: 比如，它解释了为什么必须依赖颜色，而关键直觉其实归结为：如果你不擅长推秋千上的孩子，会发生什么。耐心听我说。我保证后面就讲得通了。

cues.en: Also, when I mentioned on Patreon the intention to cover this topic, a lot of people had a lot of questions about the index of refraction. For example, numerous people asked about how it's possible for this number to be lower than one, which really does happen despite that seeming to imply the impossibility of something traveling faster than the speed of light. There was also a question about birefringence,
cues.zh: 另外，我在 Patreon 上提到打算讲这个主题时，很多人对折射率提了很多问题。比如，很多人问这个数值怎么可能小于 1——这确实会发生，尽管它似乎意味着会有东西超光速，而这按理说不可能。还有人问到了双折射，

cues.en: which is where a material can have two different indices of refraction causing you to see double when you look through it. And that actually ties in really nicely to putting in the final puzzle piece from the last two videos about the barber pole phenomenon.
cues.zh: 也就是一种材料可以有两个不同的折射率，导致你透过它看东西时看到重影。而这正好能和前两期视频里关于理发店灯柱现象的最后一块拼图衔接起来。

cues.en: And a couple people also asked about why light slowing down would imply a bending like this. And I agree that deserves a better explanation than the tank analogy. I promise we will get to all of these questions later, but it makes sense to first lay down some groundwork by spending the bulk of our time on the key question of why passing through a medium would change the speed of a light wave at all. And for this, I want you to think of your material, like glass, as being broken up into a bunch of distinct layers
cues.zh: 还有几个人问，为什么光速变慢会导致这样的弯折。我也同意，这值得比水箱类比更好的解释。我保证之后会回答所有这些问题，但先打些基础是合理的：把大部分时间花在一个关键问题上——为什么穿过介质竟会改变光波的速度。为此，我想让你把材料，比如玻璃，想成被分成许多不同的层

cues.en: all perpendicular to the direction the light is traveling. And we'll start by focusing our attention on the effect of just one of those layers on the light wave.
cues.zh: 这些层都垂直于光传播的方向。我们先集中看其中一层对光波的影响。

cues.en: The true effect would be minuscule, but if you'll let me exaggerate it for a moment, what it does is kick back the phase of the wave.
cues.zh: 真实效应会非常微小，但如果你允许我稍微夸张一下，它做的是把波的相位往回踢。

cues.en: And maybe it's worth a brief aside to make sure we're all on the same page when it comes to wave terminology.
cues.zh: 也许值得短暂岔开一下，确保大家对波的术语理解一致。

cues.en: If you go and graph the function sin of x, when you put some term in front of it affecting how high that wave oscillates up and down, that's what we call the amplitude.
cues.zh: 如果你画出函数 sin x 的图像，在它前面乘上一个项，影响波上下振荡的高度，这就是我们所说的振幅。

cues.en: When you put a term in front of x,
cues.zh: 当你在 x 前面放一个项，

cues.en: this will affect how rapidly it oscillates.
cues.zh: 这会影响它振荡的快慢。

cues.en: If this is meant to describe a wave over time, that term would be called the angular frequency.
cues.zh: 如果这是用来描述随时间变化的波，那个项就叫角频率。

cues.en: Whereas if it's meant to describe a wave over space, that constant would be called the wave number. Then if you were to add some other constant inside that sine function, and notice how as you change what that constant is, it sort of slides the wave left and right, That term describes the phase of the wave.
cues.zh: 而如果它是用来描述空间中的波，那个常数就叫波数。然后，如果你在那个正弦函数里再加上另一个常数，注意当你改变这个常数时，它会把波左右平移，这个项描述的就是波的相位。

cues.en: So when I say that our light wave hitting a layer of glass causes its phase to get kicked back, I mean if you take whatever function describes it before it hits the glass, then the function describing it after that looks almost the same, just with a little extra something added to the input of that sine function. Like I said, in reality that'll be a very small number, something proportional to the infinitesimal thickness of that layer, but I'll keep drawing it as something exaggerated and keep track of the value of that phase kick over here on the left.
cues.zh: 所以当我说光波打到一层玻璃上导致它的相位被往回踢时，我的意思是，如果你取击中玻璃前描述它的那个函数，那么之后描述它的函数看起来几乎一样，只是正弦函数的输入里多加了一点东西。就像我说的，现实中那会是一个非常小的数，与那层玻璃的无穷小厚度成正比，但我会继续把它画得夸张一些，并在左边记录这个相位踢变的值。

cues.en: Let's say you go and add a bunch of other layers of the glass, each one also applying their own kickback to the phase of the wave. The question for you is what does that new wave look like? If the value of that phase kick applied by each layer is something really close to zero, then the wave is hardly affected at all. But the larger that phase kick, the more the wave kind of gets squished together among all those layers.
cues.zh: 假设你再加上一堆玻璃层，每一层也会对波的相位施加各自的回踢。你要问的是，新的波会是什么样？如果每层施加的相位回踢值非常接近零，那么波几乎不受影响。但相位回踢越大，波就越会在这些层之间被挤压在一起。

cues.en: Admittedly, right here, it looks all kaleidoscopic and weird,
cues.zh: 诚然，就在这里，它看起来像万花筒一样千变万化又怪异，

cues.en: but that's really just because I have a discrete set of layers each applying an unrealistically large kick.
cues.zh: 但这其实只是因为我的层是离散的，而且每层施加的回踢大得不现实。

cues.en: Notice what happens if I smooth it out by doubling the density of layers, but having each one only apply half the phase kick.
cues.zh: 注意，如果我把层密度加倍来把它平滑化，但让每层只施加一半的相位回踢，会发生什么。

cues.en: And then I do that again. I double the density of the layers, but have each one only apply half the phase kick.
cues.zh: 然后我再做一次：把层密度加倍，但让每层只施加一半的相位回踢。

cues.en: As I continue this over and over, approaching a situation where you have a continuum of glass, each layer applying just a tiny infinitesimal phase kick, what you end up with is identical to, indistinguishable
cues.zh: 当我不断重复，逐渐逼近玻璃连续体的情况：每一层只施加极其微小的相位回踢，最终得到的结果等同于，并且无法区分于

cues.en: from a wave that's simply traveling slower,
cues.zh: 一列只是传播得更慢的波，

cues.en: oscillating up and down with the same frequency,
cues.zh: 以相同频率上下振荡，

cues.en: but with a wavelength that's been kind of scrunched up.
cues.zh: 但波长却被压短了。

cues.en: This right here is the first key idea with the index of refraction.
cues.zh: 这就是折射率背后的第一个关键思想。

cues.en: Instead of asking why does light slow down in glass, what we really need to ask is why does its interaction
cues.zh: 与其问光为什么在玻璃中变慢，我们真正需要问的是，为什么它和

cues.en: with a single layer of that glass cause a kickback to the phase of the wave?
cues.zh: 那种玻璃的单层之间的相互作用，会让波的相位发生回踢？

cues.en: And then when we wanna get quantitative and understand exactly how much the light slows down, which is critical for understanding why it depends on color, instead the real question is how strong is that phase kick?
cues.zh: 然后，当我们想进行定量分析，准确理解光速究竟减慢了多少时，而这对理解它为何取决于颜色至关重要，真正的问题其实是：这个相位突变有多强？

cues.en: From here, it's helpful to turn back to the fundamentals of what light even is. This is something we talked a lot about in the last video, but a little review never hurts. So let me go over the essentials.
cues.zh: 接下来，回到光的本质会很有帮助。上个视频里我们详细讨论过这一点，不过稍微复习一下总没坏处。让我讲讲其中的要点。

cues.en: As many of you know, light is a wave in the electromagnetic field, but here we'll just be drawing the electric field.
cues.zh: 如你们很多人所知，光是电磁场中的一种波，不过这里我们只画电场。

cues.en: The electric field associates each point in three d space with a little three-dimensional vector telling you what force would be applied to a hypothetical unit charge sitting at that point in space.
cues.zh: 电场为三维空间中的每个点对应一个小小的三维向量，表示假想的单位电荷位于该点时会受到什么力。

cues.en: The key thing going on with light is that if you have a charged particle and something causes it to wiggle up and down,
cues.zh: 光的关键在于：如果有一个带电粒子，某种原因使它上下摆动，

cues.en: that results in these propagating ripples in the electric field away from the charge. And that propagation is traveling at the speed c, the speed of light.
cues.zh: 那么电场中就会产生从电荷向外传播的涟漪。而这种传播速度是 c，也就是光速。

cues.en: Whenever those ripples happen to reach another charged particle, they cause it to wiggle up and down, albeit a little more weakly than the initial wiggle, and that in turn causes its own propagations.
cues.zh: 每当这些涟漪到达另一个带电粒子时，就会使它上下摆动，不过会比最初的摆动弱一些，而这又会引起它自身的传播。

cues.en: The way we described this in last video was that if at some point in time a charge is accelerating,
cues.zh: 上个视频中，我们这样描述这个过程：如果在某个时刻，一个电荷正在加速，

cues.en: then after a little delay, which depends on the speed c,
cues.zh: 那么经过一小段延迟，这段延迟取决于速度 c，

cues.en: the existence of that acceleration
cues.zh: 这个加速的存在

cues.en: induces a force on another charge.
cues.zh: 会在另一个电荷上产生一个力。

cues.en: We went over the specific force law describing this. It's something that can be derived downstream of Maxwell's equations. But for our purposes here, the main thing to tuck away in your mind is that the amount of time it takes that initial acceleration to cause any kind of influence elsewhere travels at exactly the speed c. And really, you should think of c not so much as the speed of light per se, but as the speed of causality.
cues.zh: 我们已经讲过描述这一点的具体力定律。它可以从 Maxwell 方程组进一步推导出来。但对我们这里的讨论来说，最需要记住的是：初始加速度要产生某种影响并传递到别处，所需的时间对应的传播速度恰好是 c。实际上，与其把 c 单纯理解为光速，不如把它看成因果关系传播的速度。

cues.en: It determines how fast any kind of influence travels. It's just that one of multiple consequences of that is that it's the speed of light. In particular, when you get a charge oscillating up and down in a nice clean sinusoidal motion, you can think of these rippling effects in the electric field as describing the force that would be applied to another charge sitting there as a result of that past acceleration.
cues.zh: 它决定了任何影响传播的速度有多快。光速只是它带来的多个结果之一。具体来说，当你让一个电荷以平滑的正弦运动上下振荡时，可以把电场中的这些波纹状变化理解为：由于之前的加速度，它会对那里另一个电荷施加相应的力。

cues.en: I will freely admit that I had a bit too much fun in that video just simulating how the electric field responds to accelerating charges, and that I'm kind of doing the same thing here. But there are two important facts for our pursuit of the index of refraction.
cues.zh: 我承认，在那期视频里模拟电场如何响应加速电荷时，我玩得有点太开心了，而我现在其实也在做类似的事情。不过，对于我们研究折射率来说，有两个重要事实。

cues.en: The first is that when you have multiple different charges oscillating up and down, the net effect on the electric field is just the sum of what it would be for each individual charge, which is kind of what you would expect. And then the way that it shakes out is that if you have a row of charges oscillating in sync with each other or for our purposes today, a plane of charges all wiggling up and down in sync within that plane,
cues.zh: 第一，当多个不同的电荷一起上下振荡时，电场受到的净影响就是每个单独电荷产生的影响之和，这其实也符合直觉。而具体来说，如果有一排电荷彼此同步地振荡，或者就我们今天的讨论而言，如果一个平面内的电荷都在平面内同步上下振荡，

cues.en: then the effects of each individual charge tend to cancel each other out in most directions
cues.zh: 那么每个电荷产生的影响会在大多数方向上彼此抵消

cues.en: except perpendicular to that plane, they actually constructively interfere.
cues.zh: 但在垂直于该平面的方向上，它们实际上会发生相长干涉。

cues.en: This is how you can get a concentrated beam of light. That's the important thing. If you have a layer of charges wiggling up and down in sync with each other, then even far away from that layer, it produces this nice sinusoidal wave in the electric field that we're so fond of drawing to represent light.
cues.zh: 这就是产生集中光束的方式，也是关键所在。如果有一层电荷同步上下振动，那么即使离这层电荷很远，它也会在电场中产生这种漂亮的波形，也就是我们常用画来代表光的正弦波。

cues.en: When I draw a light wave like this, it's really only depicting the electric field on a single one dimensional line. A more full picture of light in three dimensions would look something more like this. That tends to be a little bit busier, so usually we just draw the sine wave.
cues.zh: 当我像这样画光波时，其实只描绘了一维直线上的电场。光在三维空间中的完整图像更像是这样。不过那样画画面有点太繁琐了，所以通常我们只画正弦波。

cues.en: So thinking back to the question of why interactions with a layer of material would cause a kickback to the phase of the wave, let's start thinking it through. When a light beam enters a material like glass,
cues.zh: 回过头来看那个问题：为什么与一层材料相互作用会导致波的相位发生延迟推移？我们来仔细分析一下。当光束进入玻璃这样的材料时，

cues.en: then it causes all of the charges inside that material, you know, electrons or maybe the occasional ion to wiggle up and down in response to that light wave. You might think that adding together all the propagations from all those charges is a complete nightmare,
cues.zh: 它会引起材料内部所有的电荷——比如电子或偶现的离子——响应光波而上下振动。你可能会觉得，把所有这些电荷的传播波叠加在一起简直是一场噩梦，

cues.en: but we can think about it one layer at a time.
cues.zh: 但我们可以一层一层地来考虑。

cues.en: As the light wave causes this layer to wiggle up and down, that wiggling produces its own second order light wave at the same frequency,
cues.zh: 当光波引起这一层上下振动时，这种振动会产生一个同频率的二次光波，

cues.en: and it propagates in both directions perpendicular to that layer. The overall electric field then looks like the initial incoming light wave added together with the second order wave.
cues.zh: 它会沿着垂直于该层的两个方向传播。最终的整体电场，就表现为最初的入射光波与这个二次光波的叠加。

cues.en: By far, the most distracting part of what's going on here is everything on the left, and this actually corresponds to the light being reflected back.
cues.zh: 这里最分散注意力的，显然是左边的一切，而它对应的其实是被反射回来的光。

cues.en: And from experience, you all know that when you look at water or you look at glass, light not only goes through it, but some of it gets reflected back. And we could have a whole interesting discussion on quantifying exactly how much, but in the spirit of staying focused, will completely ignore that for today and only focus on what's happening to the right of that layer.
cues.zh: 从经验中你们都知道，当你看水或玻璃时，光不仅会穿过去，还有一部分会被反射回来。我们本来完全可以好好讨论一下到底反射了多少，但为了保持专注，今天会完全忽略这一点，只关注那一层右侧发生的事情。

cues.en: You can probably predict what I'm gonna say. It turns out that when you add that second order oscillation,
cues.zh: 你大概能猜到我要说什么。事实证明，当你加上那个二阶振荡，

cues.en: the overall effect is almost identical to the incoming light, but just shifted back in phase by a little bit. And then because many successive shifts to the phase like this are the same thing as light slowing down, this will ultimately explain the index of refraction.
cues.zh: 整体效果和入射光几乎一模一样，只是相位稍微往回偏移了一点。然后，因为许多次这样的连续相位偏移就等同于光变慢，这最终会解释折射率。

cues.en: But of course, the sufficiently curious viewers will now be raising their hands and asking why is that the effect when you add them together?
cues.zh: 当然，好奇心足够强的观众现在会举手问：为什么把它们加在一起会产生这种效果？

cues.en: And so here it might be worth a little sidebar on how to think about adding two waves together.
cues.zh: 所以这里可能值得稍微插一段，讲讲该怎么理解把两列波相加。

cues.en: If you draw some sine wave with some particular amplitude, some specific frequency, and some specific phase,
cues.zh: 如果你画一个正弦波，给它某个特定的振幅、某个特定的频率和某个特定的相位，

cues.en: and then you draw another sine wave also with its own amplitude, frequency, and phase,
cues.zh: 然后再画另一个正弦波，也同样有自己的振幅、频率和相位，

cues.en: in general, it's very hard to think about what the sum of those two waves should look like as you tweak those initial parameters.
cues.zh: 一般来说，当你调整这些初始参数时，很难想象这两列波的和应该是什么样子。

cues.en: In the specific case where the frequencies are the same, which is true for our example, the result will also look like a sine wave with that same frequency.
cues.zh: 在频率相同的特例中，也就是我们的例子，结果看起来也会是一个频率相同的正弦波。

cues.en: But even then, it's a little tricky to think about exactly how to describe that wave. It has some amplitude and some phase, and if I ask you to concretely compute both of those numbers based on the amplitudes and phases of the initial waves, it's not immediately clear how you would do that without maybe throwing a bunch of trig identities at the problem.
cues.zh: 但即便如此，要准确描述这个波还是有点棘手。它有一个振幅和一个相位；如果让你根据初始波的振幅和相位，具体计算出这两个数，恐怕得先套用一堆三角恒等式，但究竟该怎么做并不直观。

cues.en: But here's a really nice way to think about it. Imagine that first wave describes the y component of some rotating vector.
cues.zh: 不过，有一种非常好的理解方式。想象第一条波描述的是某个旋转向量的 y 分量。

cues.en: The length of that vector corresponds with the amplitude of our wave,
cues.zh: 这个向量的长度对应我们波的振幅，

cues.en: and then the initial rotation of that vector corresponds with the phase of our wave.
cues.zh: 而这个向量的初始旋转角度对应我们波的相位。

cues.en: And then similarly, think of that second wave as describing the y component of another rotating vector, where again the amplitude corresponds with the length of that vector, and the phase of the wave tells us the initial angle of that vector.
cues.zh: 类似地，把第二条波看作另一个旋转向量的 y 分量；同样，振幅对应这个向量的长度，而波的相位告诉我们这个向量的初始角度。

cues.en: Now to think about the sum of the two waves, just think about adding those two vectors tip to tail.
cues.zh: 现在，要理解两条波的和，只要想象把这两个向量首尾相接相加。

cues.en: And because they both have the same frequency as both of them rotate, their sum kind of rotates in lockstep with them.
cues.zh: 由于它们的频率相同，旋转时也保持同步，所以它们的向量和也会跟着一起旋转。

cues.en: So if you wanna think about the amplitude of our resulting wave, it comes down to the length of this vector sum, and similarly the phase corresponds to the angle of that vector sum.
cues.zh: 因此，如果要理解结果波的振幅，关键就是这个向量和的长度；同样，相位对应的就是这个向量和的角度。

cues.en: In some cases, this tells you things that you probably already knew, like if the two phases happen to be the same, then you get constructive interference, and you have a bigger wave that results. And if the phases were a 180 degrees out of sync, then you get deconstructive interference
cues.zh: 在某些情况下，这会告诉你一些你可能早就知道的事，比如如果两个相位恰好相同，就会发生相长干涉，结果得到更大的波。而如果相位相差 180 度、不同步，就会发生相消干涉，

cues.en: with a relatively small resulting wave.
cues.zh: 结果是相对较小的波。

cues.en: What's a little bit less obvious, but what's crucial for our discussion here,
cues.zh: 有一点没那么明显，但对我们的讨论至关重要：

cues.en: is that if the phase of that second wave happens to be exactly 90 degrees behind the phase of the first, so kind of a quarter cycle out of sync, and if that second wave is also very small compared to the first, then if you look at the little vector sum on the lower left, you'll notice how this means that the resulting wave is almost identical to the initial wave, but just shifted back in its phase by a tiny bit. Moreover, the size of that phase shift depends on the specific amplitude of that second wave.
cues.zh: 就是，如果第二个波的相位恰好比第一个波的相位落后 90 度，也就是大约四分之一个周期不同步，并且如果第二个波相比第一个波也非常小，那么看左下角那个小矢量和，你会注意到，这意味着合成波几乎与初始波完全相同，只是相位被向后推移了一点点。此外，这个相位偏移的大小取决于第二个波的具体振幅。

cues.en: So looking back at our previous animation where we have some wiggling charges in a layer of glass causing these second order propagations that need to be added together with the incoming light. The way it works out is that the phase of that second wave is exactly a quarter of a cycle behind the phase of the first. So when you add them together, you get this little phase shift. And then critically,
cues.zh: 所以回看之前的动画，其中玻璃层里有一些振动的电荷，产生了这些需要与入射光相加的二阶传播。结果是这样的：第二个波的相位恰好比第一个波落后四分之一个周期。所以把它们相加时，就会得到这个小小的相位偏移。而关键在于，

cues.en: the size of that phase shift is bigger when that second order wave is larger, and then smaller when that second order wave is smaller.
cues.zh: 当二阶波较大时，这个相位偏移就较大；当二阶波较小时，它就更小。

cues.en: Again, the very curious viewers will be raising their hands and saying, why does it work out to be exactly a quarter of a cycle behind?
cues.zh: 好奇的观众又会举手问：为什么结果恰好落后四分之一个周期？

cues.en: There is a very nice reason, but it's just a little too much detail for us today. If you're curious, I highly encourage you to take a look at the Feynman lectures on the matter.
cues.zh: 原因很漂亮，但今天讲就有点太细了。如果你好奇，我强烈建议你去看看 Feynman lectures 中关于这个问题的内容。

cues.en: For our purposes, step back for a second and think about what you need to explain the key question of prisms, which is why the index of refraction would depend on color at all.
cues.zh: 就我们的目的而言，先退一步想想：要解释棱镜的关键问题——折射率为什么竟然会依赖颜色——你需要什么。

cues.en: As you now know, that index depends on how much each layer of glass kicks back the phase of the wave, and that phase kick depends on the strength of the second order wave resulting from charge oscillations in a layer of that glass.
cues.zh: 如你现在所知，这个折射率取决于每层玻璃让波的相位偏移多少，而这个相位偏移又取决于那层玻璃中电荷振荡产生的二阶波的强度。

cues.en: So you need to drill in and understand exactly how much those charges wiggle in response to an incoming light wave. So let's zoom in on that layer and think of each one of those charged particles.
cues.zh: 所以你需要深入理解，这些电荷在入射光波作用下到底会抖动多少。那我们就放大那一层，想想其中的每一个带电粒子。

cues.en: And even though the specific molecular structure is gonna be something very complicated, we're gonna model each one of those charges as if it was bound to some equilibrium position
cues.zh: 尽管具体的分子结构会非常复杂，我们仍会把每个电荷都建模成仿佛被束缚在某个平衡位置

cues.en: by a spring or maybe a set of springs.
cues.zh: 由一根弹簧，或者也许一组弹簧。

cues.en: I don't mean this literally of course, I just mean if we describe the displacement of this charge from its equilibrium with a little vector x that's gonna depend on time,
cues.zh: 当然我不是字面意思，我只是说，如果我们用一个小向量 x 来描述这个电荷偏离平衡位置的位移，而 x 会随时间变化，

cues.en: then in our model, the force applied to the charge pulling it back to that equilibrium
cues.zh: 那么在我们的模型中，作用在电荷上、把它拉回平衡位置的力

cues.en: is gonna be something proportional
cues.zh: 会正比于

cues.en: to the size of that displacement
cues.zh: 那个位移的大小

cues.en: with a little proportionality constant k.
cues.zh: 比例常数为 k。

cues.en: This is the same law that governs how springs work. You might ask if that's accurate, and the idea is that for very small displacements,
cues.zh: 弹簧的工作原理也是遵循这条定律。你可能会问这准不准，其实在微小位移下，

cues.en: it's actually a really good approximation.
cues.zh: 它确实是一个非常好的近似。

cues.en: This is a very common thing to do throughout physics. We would call it a linear restoring force. The idea is that maybe the actual force law depends on the position in a much more complicated way, but we're basically taking a low order approximation near the equilibrium.
cues.zh: 这在物理学中非常常见，我们称之为线性回复力。也就是说，实际的受力规律与位置的关系可能复杂得多，但我们基本只是在平衡点附近做了低阶近似。

cues.en: If I just run this as a simulation plugging in this force law, here's what that displacement looks like as a function of time.
cues.zh: 如果把这个受力定律代入并运行模拟，位移随时间变化的曲线就是这样的。

cues.en: What you get looks like a sine wave. This is called simple harmonic motion, and the frequency of this wave is gonna matter a lot for you and me, and finding that comes down to solving a certain differential equation because the force is really the same thing as mass times acceleration,
cues.zh: 得到的结果看起来像个正弦波。这叫做简谐运动，而这个波的频率对我们至关重要；求这个频率归根结底要解一个微分方程，因为力本质上就是质量乘以加速度，

cues.en: and the acceleration is the same thing as the second derivative
cues.zh: 而加速度就是

cues.en: of that displacement.
cues.zh: 该位移的二阶导数。

cues.en: So what we're saying is we want some function whose second derivative looks like a certain constant times that function itself.
cues.zh: 所以我们其实是要找一个函数，它的二阶导数等于某个常数乘以它本身。

cues.en: Any differential equation students among you might enjoy thinking about how you solve this. I won't go over the full details, but the answer is reasonably intuitive, and anyone who knows a little calculus can just check it for themselves.
cues.zh: 你们当中学过微分方程的人可能会乐于思考如何求解。我就不细讲了，不过答案相当直观，任何懂点微积分的人都可以自己验证。

cues.en: The way it shakes out is that if the initial condition is that our little charge has a velocity of zero, but it's offset from the equilibrium by a little vector x naught, then the way it evolves over time looks like x naught multiplied by a cosine expression.
cues.zh: 结果是，如果初始条件是这个小电荷速度为零，但偏离平衡位置一个小向量x0，那么它随时间的演化就是x0乘以一个余弦表达式。

cues.en: So the amplitude of this wave is kind of uninteresting. It just depends on how far we pulled things back originally, but the meat is this frequency term, square root of k divided by m.
cues.zh: 所以这个波的振幅没什么意思。它只取决于我们最初把物体拉回了多远，真正关键的是这个频率项，即k除以m的平方根。

cues.en: And if you think about it, this should hopefully be at least a little intuitive.
cues.zh: 仔细想想，这至少应该有点直观。

cues.en: For example, if you increase k,
cues.zh: 比如，如果你增大k，

cues.en: which is kind of like increasing the strength of that spring,
cues.zh: 这相当于增大弹簧的强度，

cues.en: then it results in a faster oscillation.
cues.zh: 那么振荡就会更快。

cues.en: Whereas if you increase m, the mass of the particle, there's a lot more inertia and it results in a slower oscillation.
cues.zh: 而如果你增大m，也就是粒子的质量，惯性就大得多，振荡就会更慢。

cues.en: This term square root of k divided by m has a special name. It's called the resonant frequency for our simple harmonic oscillator.
cues.zh: 这个k除以m的平方根有个专门的名字，叫做简谐振子的共振频率。

cues.en: And being a little more precise, should call this the resonant angular frequency.
cues.zh: 更精确地说，应该叫它共振角频率。

cues.en: This is always a little bit of an awkwardness with physics where whenever you have some kind of cyclic process,
cues.zh: 物理学里总有点别扭的地方：每当你遇到某种周期性过程，

cues.en: when you give an intuitive description, it's natural to phrase things in terms of the frequency, the number of cycles that this process makes per unit time. But when doing math, it's often more natural to talk about the angular frequency, which you could think of as describing how much angle this process covers in radians per unit time. It's just the same as the frequency but multiplied by two pi. So for example, if you have something like a cosine expression, which you might think of as describing the x component of a cycling vector like this, then the term sitting right in front of the t in that cosine
cues.zh: 做直观描述时，自然会用频率来表述，也就是这个过程单位时间内完成的周期数。但做数学时，往往更自然的是讨论角频率，你可以把它理解为描述这个过程单位时间内转过多少弧度的角度。它就是频率乘以2π。比如，如果你有一个余弦表达式，你可以把它看作描述这样一个旋转向量的x分量，那么这个余弦里t前面的项

cues.en: is the angular frequency.
cues.zh: 就是角频率。

cues.en: This is why angular frequency makes the math a little cleaner. For example, in our simple harmonic motion, the term sitting in front of t looks like the square root of k divided by m, which I'm writing as omega sub r.
cues.zh: 这就是角频率让数学变得更简洁的原因。比如在简谐运动中，t 前面的那一项看起来像是 k 除以 m 的平方根，我把它写成 omega 下标 r。这也就是为什么角频率能让数学表达更干净。举例来说，在我们这个简谐运动里，位于 t 前面的项看起来就是 k 除以 m 的平方根，我把它写作 omega 下标 r。

cues.en: Let's package all of that up and call that our solution in the simple case where there's no external force acting on our charged particle.
cues.zh: 让我们把所有这些打包起来，称之为在没有外力作用于带电粒子时的简单情况下的解决方案。

cues.en: But of course, what we're interested in is what happens when you shine a beam of light on this material,
cues.zh: 当然，我们感兴趣的是，当一束光照射到这种材料上时会发生什么，

cues.en: which intuitively causes this charge to jiggle, but the question is how much?
cues.zh: 这直观上会让电荷晃动，但问题是晃多少？

cues.en: In our equation, this looks like adding a new force term corresponding to the light wave. That force oscillates up and down also according to some kind of cosine function,
cues.zh: 在我们的方程里，这看起来就像是增加了一个对应于光波的新力项。这个力也按照某种余弦函数上下振荡，

cues.en: but this time with a distinct angular frequency that I'm gonna call omega sub l.
cues.zh: 但这次用的是不同的角频率，我把它叫做 omega 下标 l。

cues.en: E naught here describes the strength of the wave, and then q describes the charge of whatever particle we're modeling.
cues.zh: 这里的 E naught 描述波的强度，而 q 描述我们建模的粒子的电荷。

cues.en: As usual, it's a lot easier to think about when we only draw a subset of that light wave. And in this case, we're gonna draw it on the plane of the layer of material that we care about. You might think of gusts of wind blowing our little ball on the spring up and down in a clean sinusoidal
cues.zh:
和往常一样，当我们只画出光波的一个子集时，理解起来就会容易得多。
@@
在这个例子中，我们把它画在我们关心的材料层平面上。
@@
你可能会觉得，阵风正吹着我们弹簧上的小球，使其做干净的正弦上下运动

cues.en: pattern.
cues.zh: 模式。

cues.en: Or as another analogy, it's similar to pushing a child on a swing. The swing would oscillate on its own due to the force of gravity, but you as the pusher are applying an external force which itself is oscillating over time.
cues.zh: 或者换个比喻，这就好比推一个荡秋千的小孩。秋千本身会受重力影响而摆动，但你作为推手，施加的是一个随时间振荡的外力。

cues.en: Although a key difference here is that the frequency of that external force in general has nothing to do with the resonant frequency of that little oscillator.
cues.zh: 不过这里的一个关键区别在于，外力的频率通常和微振子的共振频率毫无关系。

cues.en: The better analogy would be if you're pushing the child on the swing with a cyclic force that has nothing to do with what the swing naturally wants to do.
cues.zh: 打个更好的比方，就像你推荡秋千的孩子时，施加的周期性推力和秋千本身的固有摆动节奏完全不合拍。

cues.en: And my favorite part in literally trying to do this with my niece is that at some point she gently murmurs to herself, this isn't how mom does it.
cues.zh: 我真的和我侄女试过这么做，最逗的是，她中途小声嘀咕了一句：“妈妈才不是这么推的。”

cues.en: Now in trying to understand how much our charge is oscillating in response to the incoming light, let me start by just simulating it and plotting the result.
cues.zh: 现在为了搞清楚电荷在入射光的作用下振动得有多剧烈，我们先来做个模拟并把结果画出来。

cues.en: You'll notice that there's a little startup period where it kind of has to get going, but then after that, mercifully,
cues.zh: 你会注意到它一开始有个启动阶段，需要调整适应一下，但谢天谢地，在那之后，

cues.en: it looks nice and clean just like another sine wave. Now you might be thinking, yeah. Yeah. Everything is sine waves, but it's important to understand that this one has a very different character from the sine wave we saw earlier.
cues.zh: 图像就变得规整干脆，看起来就像另一个正弦波。你可能会想，行了行了，万物皆正弦波，但必须明确的是，这个正弦波和我们之前看到的特性截然不同。

cues.en: Earlier, without any external forces,
cues.zh: 之前在没有任何外力的情况下，

cues.en: the frequency of that wave came down to the spring constant and the mass,
cues.zh: 那个波的频率取决于弹簧劲度系数和质量，

cues.en: which is to say it depends exclusively on material properties of the glass. By contrast, with this external cycling driving force, the frequency in that steady state is the same as the frequency of the light. And then in our first case, the amplitude of the wave was kind of uninteresting. It just depends on how far you pulled the spring out to begin with. But in the second case, the amplitude of this wave is actually where all the interesting stuff happens.
cues.zh: 也就是说，它完全取决于玻璃的材料属性。相比之下，有了这个周期性的外部驱动力，稳态下的频率就和光的频率完全一致了。此外在第一种情况下，波的振幅其实没什么看头，仅仅取决于你一开始把弹簧拉开了多远。但在第二种情况下，这个波的振幅才是所有奥妙的所在。

cues.en: Exactly how much will this charge be oscillating
cues.zh: 这个电荷究竟会如何振荡

cues.en: in response to the light wave?
cues.zh: 来响应光波？

cues.en: Again, I won't go over the full details of solving this, but any eager calculus students among you might enjoy going through the exercise where if you just guess that a solution looks like a cosine wave with the same frequency as the light, and you solve for the amplitude,
cues.zh: 同样，我不会详述求解过程，不过如果你对微积分充满热情，可以尝试这样一道练习：假设解是一个与光频相同的余弦波，然后求出振幅，

cues.en: you can get a concrete solution to this equation that looks like this.
cues.zh: 你就能得到这个方程的一个具体解，形如这样。

cues.en: This is worth unpacking for a bit, and just to be clear, this is only describing things in the steady state after things have kind of gotten up and going. A fully descriptive solution would be notably more complicated.
cues.zh: 这很值得细细分析一下，需要明确的是，这描述的仅仅是系统启动并进入稳定状态之后的情况。一个完整的解会显著复杂得多。

cues.en: As I said, everything interesting here comes down to the amplitude,
cues.zh: 正如我所说，这里所有有趣的地方都归结于振幅，

cues.en: which here looks like a large collection of constants,
cues.zh: 它在这里看起来像是一大堆常数，

cues.en: most of which should be pretty intuitive if you take a moment to think about it. For example, it is proportional to the strength of that incoming light wave, so the stronger the light, the more the oscillations.
cues.zh: 只要你花点时间思考一下，其中大多数应该都相当直观。例如，它与入射光波的强度成正比，所以光越强，振荡就越剧烈。

cues.en: It's also proportional to the charge, which again makes sense, And the real heart of the matter comes down to what's sitting in the denominator here, the difference between the square of the resonant frequency and the square of the light frequency.
cues.zh: 它也与电荷成正比，这同样很好理解，而整个问题的真正核心在于分母中的这一项，即谐振频率的平方与光频的平方之差。

cues.en: And to build a little intuition,
cues.zh: 为了培养一些直观的感觉，

cues.en: take a moment to think about what would happen if the frequency of the incoming light was something very close to the resonant frequency of this oscillator.
cues.zh: 大家可以想一想，如果入射光的频率非常接近这个振荡器的谐振频率，会发生什么。

cues.en: This is analogous to the normal situation pushing a child on a swing where the frequency of your force lines up quite closely with what the swing wants to do.
cues.zh: 这就像正常推小孩荡秋千一样，你施力的频率和秋千自身的频率非常契合。

cues.en: In this case, running the simulation,
cues.zh: 在这个例子中，运行这个仿真，

cues.en: notice how the oscillations of that particle will grow and grow and grow, becoming quite large over time.
cues.zh: 注意这个粒子的振荡是如何不断增强的，随着时间推移变得相当大。

cues.en: Some of you may know the famous example of the Millennium Bridge in London, where on its opening day, it started oscillating way more than the engineers expected it to. And what was going on is that the frequency of the steps of the crowd lined up very closely with a resonant frequency causing this worryingly high amplitude.
cues.zh: 你们有些人可能知道伦敦千禧桥的著名例子，在它开通的第一天，桥面开始剧烈振荡，超出了工程师们的预期。当时的情况是，人群脚步的频率与共振频率高度重合，导致了令人担忧的高振幅。

cues.en: By contrast, notice what happens in the simulation if the frequency of the light, omega sub l, is something much smaller than the resonant frequency.
cues.zh: 相比之下，注意在仿真中，如果光的频率（即 $\omega_l$）远小于共振频率会发生什么。

cues.en: For this particular simulation, it takes a little bit of a moment before things get into their full swing. Eventually, it finds a nice sinusoidal motion,
cues.zh: 对于这个特定的仿真，需要稍等一会儿，情况才会完全进入状态。最终，它会呈现出漂亮的简谐运动，

cues.en: but the amplitude of that motion is much more modest in comparison.
cues.zh: 但相比之下，这种运动的振幅要小得多。

cues.en: So what our equation is telling us is that the larger the difference between those frequencies,
cues.zh: 所以我们的公式告诉我们，这两个频率之间的差值越大，

cues.en: then the bigger the denominator,
cues.zh: 分母就会越大，

cues.en: so the smaller the overall wiggle to that charge. And again, this is something you can see in the footage with my niece. As I'm applying a force with a frequency that's very different from what the swing wants to do, she ends up oscillating at the same frequency as my force,
cues.zh: 因此这个电荷的总抖动就会越小。同样地，你可以从我侄女的视频片段中看到这一点。当我施加一个与秋千自身频率截然不同的力的频率时，她最后会以我施力的频率进行振荡，

cues.en: but she's going at a relatively low amplitude.
cues.zh: 但她的振幅相对较低。

cues.en: Stepping back, what this means is that as you shine light into a material like glass, it's not just that it induces wiggles in the charges of that material,
cues.zh: 退一步说，这意味着当你把光照射到玻璃这样的材料中时，它不仅仅是在该材料的电荷中引起振荡，

cues.en: but the specific size of those wiggles
cues.zh: 而且这些振荡的具体幅度

cues.en: depends on the frequency of the light as a consequence of this denominator term. And the more those wiggle, the bigger the size of the second order wave caused by that layer, which in turn causes a bigger shift to the phase of the overall wave.
cues.zh: 取决于光的频率，这是由分母项决定的。振荡越剧烈，该层产生的二阶波幅度就越大，进而对整体波的相位造成更大的偏移。

cues.en: Because a lot of different shifts to the phase are what causes this apparent slowdown to the light, it means that the amount that it will slow down ultimately depends on the frequency of the light.
cues.zh: 因为正是大量不同的相位偏移导致了光看起来变慢，这意味着它减速的程度最终取决于光的频率。

cues.en: So that is the real reason why prisms work. You cannot truly explain the light separation until you get down to the driven harmonic oscillator.
cues.zh: 所以这才是棱镜起作用的真正原因。不深入到受驱谐振子，你就无法真正解释光的分离。

cues.en: Now, I have left out a number of details,
cues.zh: 现在，我略去了一些细节，

cues.en: and again, I encourage the curious viewers to take a look at the Feynman lectures that a lot of this is based on. One quite important detail that would be a little criminal not to mention is that when we're modeling our charge as a little harmonic oscillator with this linear restoring force,
cues.zh: 再次鼓励好奇的观众去看看费曼物理学讲义，本内容很多都基于它。有一个相当重要的细节，不提就有点说不过去了：当我们将电荷建模为具有线性回复力的谐振子时，

cues.en: there should really also be a term that depends on the velocity of that charge. You might think of this as a kind of drag force.
cues.zh: 实际上还应该有一个依赖于该电荷速度的项。你可以把它想成一种阻力。

cues.en: This term accounts for the fact that energy from the incoming light wave is absorbed by the material.
cues.zh: 这一项解释了入射光波的能量被材料吸收这一事实。

cues.en: Without it, this whole explanation would seem to imply that light always passes through every material, not just glass and water. When as you can tell just by looking around, there's all sorts of materials for which light is mostly reflected and absorbed.
cues.zh: 如果没有这个解释，整段话听起来就像是光能穿透所有物质，而不仅仅是玻璃和水。但正如你环顾四周所见，有很多物质对光主要是反射和吸收。

cues.en: As I mentioned at the start, folks on Patreon had numerous questions about the index of refraction, like how it can be less than one and why slowing implies bending. So I made a supplemental video answering a handful of those questions, which should be published in just a few days.
cues.zh: 正如我在开头所提到的，Patreon 上的朋友们对折射率提出了很多问题，比如它怎么会小于 1，以及为什么减速意味着弯曲。所以我做了一个补充视频来回答其中几个问题，应该会在几天内发布。

cues.en: In the meantime, my friend, Mithana, from the channel Looking Glass Universe, just put out a pair of videos on the related, but definitely distinct question
cues.zh: 与此同时，我的朋友 Mithana，也就是 Looking Glass Universe 频道的创作者，刚刚发布了两个视频，探讨了一个相关但截然不同的问题：

cues.en: of whether light slows down in a medium, not in the sense of following the crests of a clean pure sine wave in a steady state, but in the sense of trying to send information through that medium,
cues.zh: 光在介质中是否会减速。这里指的不是在稳定状态下追踪纯净正弦波的波峰，而是指试图通过该介质传输信息的情况，

cues.en: like with a little wave packet. I definitely owe the existence of this video to many conversations with her about this topic,
cues.zh: 比如通过一个小波包。这个视频的诞生绝对要归功于我和她关于这个话题的多次交流，

cues.en: and viewers here will definitely enjoy taking a look, especially at the second one.
cues.zh: 这里的观众一定会喜欢看的，特别是第二个视频。

cues.en: By the way, some collaborators and I made this notebook that I think a lot of viewers might enjoy. And given that it's the holiday season, it seems worth a quick mention. The premise is that every one of the pages has a quote that's related to math and I had a lot of fun curating them all, trying to constrain myself to quotes conveying some genuinely thought provoking idea.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我和一些合作者制作了这个笔记本，我觉得很多观众会喜欢。考虑到现在是假期，我觉得值得顺便提一下。它的前提是每一页都有一句与数学相关的引言，我在整理这些引言时乐在其中，并尽量限制自己只挑选那些传达真正引人深思的想法的名言。

cues.en: And then aside from the content, I basically made the kind of notebook that I most enjoy taking notes in. Something that's readily portable with very faint grid lines helpful for diagrams, but otherwise unobtrusive.
cues.zh: 除了内容本身，我其实做了这么一本我最喜欢拿来记笔记的本子：轻巧便携，网格线非常淡，方便画图，平时又毫不碍眼。

cues.en: All bound in this nice soft faux leather. If that seems up your alley, can find them in the three blue one brown store next to a lot of other mathematical merchandise.
cues.zh: 全都用手感极佳的柔软仿皮装订。如果你也感兴趣，可以在 3Blue1Brown 商店找到它，旁边还有很多其他数学周边。
